evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents a rare Nomad Super Fuzz whose internal circuit reportedly matches a late-1966/early-1967 germanium Mosrite Fuzzrite. The enclosure retains original Fuzzrite-style labeling and a Nomad logo, making a factory OEM relationship plausible, but the connection between Nomad/LIMMCO and Mosrite is not established. Do not assign this pedal to Applied Audio merely because later Nomad products were Applied-built.

Current evidence does not demonstrate that Applied Audio built the early germanium Fuzzrite-related Nomad Super Fuzz. Tone Machines treats the early supplier connection as unresolved. Later Nomad Banshee and Rogue fuzzes were Applied-built, but that cannot be retroactively applied to the Super Fuzz.

The Nomad name is now documented across multiple supplier states: an unresolved early Super Fuzz, later Applied Audio Banshee and Rogue products, and a UMI-linked Tone Booster. The brand name itself cannot be used as a factory shortcut.

Effects Database groups Gracin's Fubar with the flat-triangle three-knob East Coast Fuzz variants. Tone Machines notes distinctive 94047 transistors and construction similarities with other East Coast examples and Andre products. This supports family association but does not identify a confirmed physical manufacturer. Keep separate from the Foxx-made Gracin's & Towne Wa & Volume product.
